title: Monotonicity conjecture for hook counts in t-regular partitions
statement:
For integers $t\geq2$ and $k\geq1$, let $b_{t,k}(n)$ denote the number of hooks of length $k$ in all $t$-regular partitions of $n$. A $t$-regular partition is a partition with no part divisible by $t$.

**Monotonicity conjecture.** Let $t\geq3$ be an integer. Then

$$
b_{t+1,2}(n)\geq b_{t,2}(n),
$$

for all $n\geq0$.

The conjecture formalizes numerical evidence that the number of hooks of length $2$ in $t$-regular partitions increases with $t$. The source gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2006.07704](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.07704), [arXiv:1808.01416](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.01416).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.15088

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).
source_name: Gurinder Singh and Rupam Barman, “Hook length inequalities for t-regular partitions in the t-aspect”, arXiv:2410.15088 (2025).
